label: WEEKEND MARKET SYNTHESIS
title: IT led the rebound. Company results still diverge.
summary: Market coverage reported a stronger close on Friday 16 October, with IT among the leaders. The Q2 filings show why that rally needs a company-by-company read: Tech Mahindra reported firmer growth and deal wins, while Wipro’s revenue growth was modest and bookings fell sequentially.

observations.label: MARKET TONE · FRIDAY 16 OCT
observations.title: The IT-led rebound carried into Friday
observations.text: Financial Express reported Indian benchmarks finishing higher, with IT among the leading sectors. This is useful short-window context; it does not prove that the advance is broad or durable. No index quote series is republished here.
observations.readThrough: A sector-led session can conceal uneven participation. One or two strong days are not a buy signal for every IT stock.

observations.label: EARNINGS · Q2 FY27
observations.title: Results support selectivity, not a blanket sector call
observations.text: Tech Mahindra reported 7.2% year-on-year constant-currency revenue growth, a 14.8% EBIT margin (about 40 basis points higher quarter on quarter), and deal wins up 25.4% year on year. Wipro reported 0.6% year-on-year constant-currency growth in IT services revenue; total bookings were down 22.9% quarter on quarter in constant currency.
observations.readThrough: These are issuer-reported company measures with different definitions. Track whether bookings convert into revenue and whether growth holds; do not rank the firms from one quarter alone.

earnings.footnote: EBIT margin 14.8%, up about 40 bps QoQ; deal wins TCV up 25.4% YoY.

earnings.metricLabel: IT services revenue growth · YoY CC
earnings.footnote: Total bookings down 22.9% QoQ CC; IT services operating margin 16.5%, up 0.5 percentage points QoQ.

implication: Research opinion: do not chase the IT rally. The current repository has no live valuations or current prices, so it cannot support a fresh stock-specific buy price or a current portfolio return.
planView: Your reported principal is ₹9,380.70 of October’s ₹10,000 allocation; ₹619.30 remains unallocated before fees. That is already 93.8% of this month’s tranche. No forced sixth position is justified by the saved market and earnings evidence. Carry the small balance to the next review or consider a diversified addition only after checking current price, valuation and execution costs. The remaining ₹90,000 belongs to future monthly tranches, not today’s brokerage cash.
